newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says troops to leave Albania by August 12.
newsitem.headline: Italy says troops to leave Albania by August 12.

text.p: Italy's Defence Chief of Staff, Admiral Guido Venturoni, said on Monday that a multinational security force Italy is leading in Albania would withdraw completely from the Balkan country by August 12.
Venturoni, commander of the 7,000-strong force, told reporters the troop withdrawal would begin on July 20 and would be finished within 20 days "if there are no complications".
Venturoni told reporters at a book presentation that by August 12, he expected the troops to be "all out".

The 11-nation force deployed in April to safeguard the distribution of aid and secure elections held on June 29 and July 6 after Europe's poorest country was swept into anarchy following the collapse of popular but dubious savings schemes.

The United Nations agreed a 45-day extension of the force's mandate on June 19 after its original term expired on June 28. The extension was requested by Albania's national unity government, installed to restore stability in the run-up to elections that were supposed to end months of mayhem.

Albania's ex-communist Socialists prepared on Monday to form a new government after a landslide victory that looked set to give them a two-thirds majority in parliament over the right-wing Democrats of outgoing President Sali Berisha.
